item.text: {"search_note":"I found clear official evidence that social benefits were routed through formal institutions, but I did not find an independent 2023 audit showing that social-service ministries were insulated from patronage in hiring, procurement, or regional allocation. The strongest independent evidence instead describes corruption, politicization, and loyalty-based management, so the pro case remains mostly procedural rather than substantive.","evidence":[{"title":"Special social payments for medical workers","publisher":"Government of the Russian Federation","date":"9 Jan 2023","url":"https://government.ru/en/news/47503/","summary":"The government said special payments for primary-care, ambulance, rural, and remote-area medical staff would start on 1 Jan 2023, be calculated from hours worked, and be administered through the Social Fund with electronic employee lists and portal notifications. That is strong evidence of a structured administrative channel rather than ad hoc patronage.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.2"]},{"title":"Single child-benefit administration","publisher":"Government of the Russian Federation","date":"9 Jan 2023","url":"https://government.ru/en/news/47503/","summary":"The same government decision said lump-sum family benefits for birth, child-rearing, and low-income pregnant women began on 1 Jan and were administered as a single payment stream. This supports a centralized, rule-based benefits system for families with children.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.2"]},{"title":"School buses, free meals, and teacher pay support in 2023","publisher":"Government of the Russian Federation","date":"2024 retrospective on 2023","url":"https://government.ru/en/news/51246/","summary":"The government reported nearly 3,000 school buses delivered in 2023, free hot meals for all primary pupils, and bonus pay for teachers and educational advisers. This is evidence of organized education-service delivery, though the source is official self-report.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.2"]},{"title":"Official wage monitoring for social-sector workers","publisher":"Rosstat","date":"2024","url":"https://rosstat.gov.ru/storage/mediabank/itog-monitor_04-2023.htm","summary":"Rosstat published 2023 wage monitoring for teachers, doctors, social workers, and other social-sphere staff. That shows a functioning statistical bureaucracy tracking social-service labor inputs, but it is only weak evidence of quality management.","question_ids":["6B.4"]},{"title":"Corruption remains pervasive and politicized","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2023","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023","summary":"Freedom House says corruption is pervasive, officials use positions to amass property, the state imposes takeovers and large tax penalties on selected firms, and access to economic statistics is restricted. That points strongly toward capture and patronage rather than neutral professional administration.","question_ids":["6B.4"]},{"title":"Education was politicized through patriotic instruction","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2023","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023","summary":"Freedom House says schools and teachers were ordered to run patriotic-education classes, use state-sanctioned language about the invasion, and comply with military-training directives; educators who dissented were fined or dismissed. This is direct evidence that a core social service was subordinated to political loyalty.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.1"]},{"title":"Governance remained personalist and patronage-based","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2023","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2023","summary":"Freedom House describes Putin’s system as personalist, with civil society forced into pro-state tasks and government support coming with strings attached. That is a broad but relevant indicator that social-sector funding was embedded in patronage politics.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.1"]},{"title":"Impunity and repression undercut professional oversight","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","date":"22 Apr 2024","url":"https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia","summary":"The report says authorities jailed antiwar protesters and opposition figures, forced NGO closures, restricted media, and left impunity intact for security personnel. That implies weak institutional accountability for public administration, including social services.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.1"]}]}
